title: Enhancing Online Continual Learning with Plug-and-Play State Space Model and Class-Conditional Mixture of Discretization
caption: Figure 1. Framework of S6MOD. Our method (a) introduces a plug-and-play branch after the backbone, where features are learned through S6MOD and supervised by the ETF classiﬁer to guide the base method. S6MOD (c) utilizes MoE to enhance the discretization of SSM and applies class-conditional routing (b) to dynamically adjust the discretization based on the uncertainty. Finally, we use a contrastive discretization loss (d) to supervise the learning of both generalizable and discriminative features.

title: STDDNet: Harnessing Mamba for Video Polyp Segmentation via Spatial-aligned Temporal Modeling and Discriminative Dynamic Representation Learning
caption: Figure 2. Overview of STDDNet, which consists of a spatial-aligned temporal dependency propagation (STDP) module and a discrimina- tive dynamic feature extraction (DDFE) module. STDP takes compressed high-level features from a pretrained image backbone as input, and utilizes Mamba temporally to model temporal consistency across consecutive frames. DDFE employs Mamba spatially to extract structural feature from multi-frame inputs, complemented by a gated dynamic activation unit (GDAU) to explore frame-wise dynamic variations. Based on enhanced spatiotemporal and dynamic features, STDDNet generates refined polyp segmentation results.

Information from CSWA and ISCA is aggregated by FEFN using the asymmetric activation mechanism.

title: Towards Multi-modal Transformers in Federated Learning
caption: Fig. 2: Overview of our proposed framework, FedCola. In each round of FL, uni- modal clients download the global model for their modality along with the transformer blocks from the other modalities and perform complementary local training to address the cross-modality gap, while multi-modal clients perform standard multi-modal local training. Then, all clients send their local updates to the server for uni-aggregation and collaborative aggregation to address the in-modality gap.

title: SAPT : A Shared Attention Framework for Parameter-Efficient Continual Learning of Large Language Models
caption: Figure 2: The overall architecture of our proposed SAPT. We assume that SAPT is currently at the time step 3 to learn the task T3. (1) In the SALS, as illustrated by the solid lines, the resulting attention weight a3 of task T3 is first obtained via the instance-level shared attention operation between the input x3 and PET key vectors {k1, k2, k3}, to perform weighted combination of all PET blocks {B1, B2, B3} for the attentive learning of the current task T3. And dashed lines display the process of attentive selection, following the same process of shared attention to reach the attention weight a3 and utilizing it to handle given inputs at the testing time. (2) In the ARM, for previous tasks T1 and T2, the current attention weights of them ( ˆa1 and ˆa2), are pulled back to their original states (a1 and a2), with the introduction of generated pseudo samples ˆx1 and ˆx2.

title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
caption: Figure 1: Model overview. We split an image into ﬁxed-size patches, linearly embed each of them, add position embeddings, and feed the resulting sequence of vectors to a standard Transformer encoder. In order to perform classiﬁcation, we use the standard approach of adding an extra learnable “classiﬁcation token” to the sequence. The illustration of the Transformer encoder was inspired by Vaswani et al. (2017).
